entries.title: mcp-preflight — static migration-readiness checker for the MCP 2026-07-28 spec
mcp-chaos — fault-injecting MCP proxy and agent resilience scorer
skill-collider — LLM-free static routing-collision analyzer for Agent Skills (SKILL.md)
context-xray - LLM-free static perception-gap scanner for MCP tool manifests & Agent Skills (invisible-Unicode smuggling, hidden markup, injection intent)
forkpoint - LLM-free behavioral fork-point analyzer that localizes where AI agents diverge across repeated same-task runs (OpenTelemetry gen_ai traces)

loadout - LLM-free budget-constrained progressive-disclosure planner for MCP tool manifests & Agent Skills (models eager-vs-deferred tool loading as a token-budget knapsack over static keep-eager signals; emits a deployable defer_loading plan + CI gate)

overreach - LLM-free static annotation-integrity auditor for MCP tool manifests (flags tools whose declared safety hints readOnlyHint/destructiveHint/idempotentHint/openWorldHint under-state actual behavior; emits per-tool auto-approval policy + trust score + CI gate)

contravene - LLM-free variance-aware breaking-change classifier for MCP tool contracts (classifies inputSchema/outputSchema evolution as MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH using input-contravariance vs output-covariance; computes required semver bump and fails CI when the declared version bump under-states it; also flags safety-hint downgrades and the outputSchema-vs-error-result validation collision)

trifecta - LLM-free static lethal-trifecta capability-flow analyzer for MCP toolsets (classifies each tool by direction x locus into the private/untrusted/exfil legs, detects when a toolset or cross-server bundle closes the exfiltration channel, computes the minimum-cost set of tools to gate to break it, emits provably trifecta-free per-task catalogs + risk score + CI gate)

capsule - LLM-free content-addressed lockfile + supply-chain mutability auditor for agent capabilities (content-hashes Agent Skills SKILL.md bundles & MCP server configs into capsule.lock.json, statically flags unpinned npx/pip/npm installs, curl|sh RCE, mutable git/container refs, insecure http and @latest tag pins; fails CI on drift as static rug-pull detection and on hazards above a severity threshold)

gauntlet - offline, LLM-free MCP tool-contract conformance fuzzer (the series' first DYNAMIC entry: executes each MCP tool over real stdio through schema-derived valid + adversarial inputs and grades live responses against MCP result-shape invariants - outputSchema conformance, structuredContent<->TextContent mirroring (SEP-1624), isError semantics, crash/timeout/stdout-pollution, silent-accept of schema-invalid input; emits a scored report + CI exit-code gate; pure stdlib, ships a conformant reference server that scores 100/100 and a buggy server exhibiting six ground-truth bug classes)

courier - offline, LLM-free adversarial state-custody auditor for MCP Multi-Round-Trip Requests (SEP-2322): drives an MRT stdio server as the untrusted client courier the spec warns about and grades whether it protects the requestState it hands across the client trust boundary - integrity (MUST-always-validate; blind + structure-preserving tamper), confidentiality (opaque vs client-readable/secret-PII leak), user-binding (MUST bind state to the authenticated user; cross-principal replay), inputResponses schema validation, replay/idempotency (double-execution) and unbounded state-growth; emits a scored report + CI exit-code gate; pure stdlib, ships a conformant reference server (100/A) and a buggy server exhibiting six ground-truth defects incl. a confirmed money-moving tamper exploit

blackbox - offline, LLM-free passive trace-conformance verifier for the new MCP Tasks extension lifecycle (io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks, 2026-07-28 RC): the series first PASSIVE / log-analysis entry - replays a captured JSON-RPC trace against the task state machine (terminal-state immutability, completed/failed/cancelled payload contracts, the unsolicited-handle MUST-NOT, input_required/inputRequests, tasks/update input correlation, pollIntervalMs backpressure & ttl expiry) with a 23-rule catalog, scored report + CI exit-code gate; pure stdlib, ships a conformant reference trace (100/A) and a buggy trace with eight ground-truth defects

askance - offline, LLM-free elicitation-safety & conformance auditor for MCP elicitation/create (the series first entry on the human-in-the-loop elicitation channel): audits captured elicitation exchanges against the MCP 2025-06-18 elicitation contract with a 32-rule catalog in 5 families - schema legality (flat primitive-only requestedSchema subset: nesting/arrays/refs/bad formats/inconsistent enums/unknown required), the sensitive-data MUST-NOT (flags credential/PII field names + phishing messages), perception & injection (zero-width/bidi Unicode, injection markers, homoglyph field names), usability (renderable-form defects), and response-vs-schema conformance (invalid action, accept-without-content, missing required, type/enum/bounds mismatch); scored report + CI exit-code gate, pure stdlib; ships a conformant reference capture (100/A) and a buggy capture with 24 ground-truth defects, 82 tests

understudy - offline, LLM-free safety & conformance auditor for the MCP sampling channel (sampling/createMessage): the server->client 'borrow the client's LLM' inversion and structural inverse of #014's elicitation. Audits captured sampling exchanges against the 2026-07-28 contract via a 15-rule / ~30-check catalog in 6 families - deprecation & capability (SEP-2577 sampling-deprecation advisory + SEP-2596 includeContext/tools capability gating), schema & structure (required/positive maxTokens, roles/content types, tool_result no-mixing + tool_use<->tool_result balance), context confidentiality (allServers/thisServer cross-server exfiltration), injection & perception (Unit 42 injection/covert-tool signatures, zero-width/bidi Unicode, homoglyph tool names), resource abuse (maxTokens token-bomb, expensive-model steering), and human-in-the-loop & result conformance - scored report + CI exit-code gate, pure stdlib; ships a conformant reference capture (100/A) and a malicious capture with 27 ground-truth rule defects, 46 tests

deputy - offline, LLM-free authorization-flow safety & conformance auditor for the MCP authorization spec (2025-11-25): the series' first entry on the OAuth 2.1 / transport layer (every prior entry audits a message/content channel). Passively audits a captured MCP authorization handshake against a 29-rule catalog in 6 families - discovery & metadata (RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata / RFC 8414 AS-metadata / S256 advertisement), PKCE & auth-code (OAuth 2.1 mandatory S256, cryptographic code_verifier<->code_challenge check using the RFC 7636 vector, no implicit flow), resource indicators & audience (RFC 8707) incl. the flagship confused-deputy pair C6 audience-validation-failure (server honors a token whose aud is another service) + C7 token-passthrough (client token forwarded verbatim downstream), token transport & hygiene (bearer-header/no-query-string, expired-token-accepted, short-lived, scope minimization), redirect & transport security (HTTPS-only AS endpoints, loopback-or-https redirect_uri, javascript:/data:/file: URL rejection, plaintext-token exposure), and SSRF/metadata hygiene (private/cloud-metadata IPs in discovery URLs) - severity-weighted score + grade + CI exit-code gate, pure stdlib; ships a conformant reference capture (100/A) and a malicious confused-deputy-proxy capture with 20 ground-truth defects incl. a confirmed token-passthrough exfiltration exploit to a Drive-like API, 47 tests

cordon - offline, LLM-free filesystem/URI boundary-confinement auditor for the MCP roots channel (the series first entry on the roots capability - the client->server declaration of filesystem operating boundaries; every prior entry audited a message/content channel). Passively replays a captured session and grades whether the server stayed confined within the client-declared roots via a 25-rule catalog in 6 families - declaration legality (non-file:// scheme, non-absolute, empty set, overlap, in-root traversal, filesystem-root over-breadth, non-local authority), containment (a segment-boundary prefix check that rejects the EscapeRoute CVE-2025-53109 /allow_dir_sensitive string-prefix bug; the flagship out-of-root read = CRITICAL), traversal & encoding (dot-segments, percent-encoded/double-encoded traversal, backslash-on-POSIX, NUL/control chars), normalization bypass (Unicode look-alike separators, trailing dot/space, device & UNC paths, drive-relative, 8.3 short names), scheme confusion (non-file SSRF/exfil, file:// network authority) and dynamic-root lifecycle (stale/removed-root use after roots/list_changed, access-before-declared, list_changed-not-honored, capability-absent access) - severity-weighted score + grade + CI exit-code gate, pure stdlib; ships a conformant reference capture (100/A) and a malicious root-escape capture with 32 findings across 21 rules incl. a confirmed /etc/passwd read outside the declared root, 80 tests

prompter - offline, LLM-free safety & conformance auditor for the MCP prompts channel (prompts/list, prompts/get) and its companion completion channel (completion/complete): the series' first entry on the prompts capability - the one channel MCP frames as 'user-controlled', yet whose template body, argument-interpolated output, name/title/description and embedded resources are entirely server-authored and injected into the conversation under the user's (or assistant's) name as a trusted slash command. Passively replays a captured JSON-RPC session and grades whether the server weaponized the channel via a 42-rule catalog in 6 families - CAP (capability & declaration legality: prompts/completions declared before use, listChanged coherence, duplicate/empty/non-string names), ARG (argument-schema legality: duplicate args, non-boolean required, undeclared-argument acceptance, required-argument enforcement / owed -32602), INJ (interpolation & injection safety: server-authored injection markers attributed to the template via argument-residue subtraction rather than the user's typed arg, injection in name/title/description = prompt-channel tool-poisoning, a user argument echoed into an assistant-role message = words in the model's mouth, unsubstituted {{placeholder}} leaks), PERC (perception & concealment: zero-width/bidi/control/Unicode TAG-block payloads, and homoglyph prompt-name shadowing of a trusted slash command /dеploy->/deploy or of another prompt), RES (embedded-content & exfiltration: argument-steered outbound resource URIs = exfil/SSRF, off-origin & javascript:/data: schemes, malformed embedded resources, oversized blob/text token bombs, invalid roles/content-types) and CMP (completion channel & result conformance: secret/credential leakage in completion values, injection-in-suggestion, the spec's 100-value cap, total/hasMore incoherence, unknown-prompt/undeclared-argument references) - severity-weighted score + grade + CI exit-code gate, pure stdlib; ships a conformant reference capture (100/A) and a trojaned 'acmedeploy' capture with 32 findings across 29 rules and all six families incl. 4 CRITICALs (assistant-mouth injection, /deploy command-shadow, argument-steered exfil URL, AWS-key leak in a completion), 52 tests

mirage - offline, LLM-free safety & conformance auditor for the MCP resources channel (resources/list, resources/read, resources/templates/list, resources/subscribe, notifications/resources/updated & list_changed): the series first entry on the resources capability - the third core MCP primitive (alongside tools and prompts) and the only one that is subscribable, giving it a TOCTOU primitive the tool-poisoning/rug-pull literature never covers. Passively replays a captured JSON-RPC session and reconstructs a per-URI read timeline to grade whether the server weaponized the channel, via a 35-rule catalog in 6 families - CAP (capability & declaration legality: resources used-before-declared, subscribe/listChanged used-unadvertised, unsolicited resources/updated, duplicate/blank URIs), SCH (schema & structure: text/blob exclusivity, base64 validity, mimeType token legality, RFC 6570 uriTemplate legality, the new 2026-07-28 ttlMs/cacheScope fields), SUB (subscription integrity: the flagship resource rug-pull SUB01 = subscribed content swapped benign->malicious across an updated notification = TOCTOU CRITICAL, phantom subscription, update storm, silent content drift, post-approval shadow resource), URI (exfiltration & SSRF: URI01 client-variable-in-authority template = CRITICAL, dangerous scheme, cloud-metadata/private host, off-origin content, exfil-sink query param), INJ (content injection & perception: INJ01 prompt-injection in resource content = resource poisoning CRITICAL, metadata poisoning, zero-width/bidi/TAG Unicode, homoglyph name shadowing, mimeType spoof vs actual bytes) and RES (abuse & result conformance: token bomb, under-reported size, audience-steered auto-inject, read-any undeclared-URI read, pagination cursor loop/path-leak) - severity-weighted score + grade + CI exit-code gate, pure stdlib; ships a conformant reference capture (100/A) and a trojan capture with 30 findings across 29 rules and all six families incl. 4 CRITICALs (SUB01 resource rug-pull, URI01 authority-templated SSRF, two INJ01 resource-content injections), 76 tests

passport - offline, LLM-free safety & conformance auditor for the stateless MCP lifecycle (SEP-2575, MCP 2026-07-28 RC): the series' first entry on the connection lifecycle itself. The 2026-07-28 release candidate REMOVED the initialize/initialized handshake and unbundled its three jobs (protocol-version negotiation, server capabilities + the system-prompt-bound instructions string, client capabilities) into a per-request _meta credential set (io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion|clientInfo|clientCapabilities|logLevel) plus a new server/discover RPC. passport passively replays a captured stateless session and grades whether the server honored the new contract and weaponized the newly per-request credential surface, via a 34-rule catalog in 6 families - DISC (server/discover conformance: MUST-implement, DiscoverResult schema supportedVersions/capabilities/serverInfo/instructions, unknown capability keys), INJ (the relocated instructions/serverInfo injection surface: prompt-injection signatures = CRITICAL, invisible/bidi/TAG Unicode, homoglyph serverInfo.name, embedded credentials, cloud-metadata/SSRF URLs, oversized token bomb), VER (per-request version negotiation: required protocolVersion _meta, mandatory MCP-Protocol-Version header, header/_meta mismatch, the flagship per-request protocol-version DOWNGRADE that dodges a later-version MUST, -32022 UnsupportedProtocolVersionError shape, accepting a version outside supportedVersions), CAP (per-request capability coherence: required clientCapabilities, CAP02 server relied on an undeclared capability = CRITICAL, CAP03 capability inference across requests = the statelessness-forbidden 'remembering', -32021 MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError shape, clientInfo legality), STATE (statelessness invariants & removed RPCs: use of a removed RPC initialize/ping/logging.setLevel/roots.list/resources.subscribe, Mcp-Session-Id reliance, STATE03 per-request AUTH BYPASS = CRITICAL, Last-Event-ID resumable stream, removed HTTP GET endpoint, session/init-state enforcement) and STREAM (per-request logging opt-in: log notification without logLevel; subscriptions/listen: acknowledgment-first, opt-in-only notification types, subscriptionId correlation, notifications-only stream) - severity-weighted score + grade + CI exit-code gate, pure stdlib; ships a conformant reference capture (100/A) and a trojan capture with 26 findings across 23 rules and all six families incl. 3 CRITICALs (INJ01 instructions system-prompt injection, CAP02 undeclared-capability reliance, STATE03 per-request auth bypass), 91 tests

augur - offline, LLM-free safety & conformance auditor for the MCP completion channel (completion/complete): the series' first entry on the completion (autocomplete) capability — the only MCP channel whose user-interaction model is per-keystroke, so every partial argument value the user types (including secrets they never submit) is streamed to the server, and every returned suggestion is inserted into the user's input; un-deprecated by the 2026-07-28 RC (unlike Roots/Sampling/Logging). Passively replays a captured JSON-RPC session, reconstructs per-(ref,argument) keystroke timelines, and grades weaponization via a 33-rule catalog in 6 families — CAP (capability & declaration legality: completion-without-declared-capability, undeclared prompt/argument reference, invalid ref type, 2026-07-28 resultType, fabricated completions for unknown refs), LEAK (value & keystroke exfiltration, unique to this channel: LEAK01 credential captured mid-keystroke = CRITICAL, PII/private-path capture, cross-argument context leakage, full-value keystroke reconstruction, server reflecting a sensitive typed value, completion solicited on a credential-shaped argument), INJ (suggestion content injection & perception: INJ01 prompt-injection in a returned suggestion = completion poisoning CRITICAL, invisible/bidi/TAG Unicode, homoglyph/confusable characters, embedded credential, control chars), STEER (adversarial ranking & dangerous defaults: STEER01 dangerous value ranked #1 = CRITICAL, confusable typosquat ranked above the genuine value, suggestions that ignore the typed prefix), URI (resource-ref URI exfiltration & SSRF: URI01 suggested URI targets cloud-metadata/SSRF host = CRITICAL, dangerous scheme, exfil-sink query param, off-origin, client-variable-in-authority template, sensitive local path) and RES (result conformance & abuse: 100-value spec-cap overflow, non-string/duplicate/blank values, total/hasMore incoherence, oversized token-bomb payload) — severity-weighted score + grade + CI exit-code gate, pure stdlib; ships a conformant reference capture (100/A) and a trojan capture that triggers all 33 rules (38 findings across all six families incl. 5 CRITICALs: LEAK01 AWS-key keystroke capture, INJ01 suggestion injection, STEER01 dangerous default, URI01 x2 metadata SSRF), 57 tests

throughline - offline, LLM-free cross-channel taint-flow / provenance auditor for a captured MCP session: the series' first entry that audits the SEAMS BETWEEN channels rather than one channel in isolation (all prior entries 011-021 audit a single channel; #009 trifecta is static over the tool manifest and asks only whether a capability set *permits* a lethal trifecta). Builds an information-flow graph over a full multi-channel capture and detects end-to-end exfiltration/injection CHAINS no single-channel view can see — an untrusted value read on one channel (resource content, tool result, prompt body, autocomplete suggestion, borrowed-LLM sampling output) reaching a dangerous sink on ANOTHER (tool-call argument, outbound URL, sampling prompt fed back to the model, elicitation message shown to the user, resource-read URI). Deterministic, time-ordered taint propagation with significance-gated value matching (exact / whole-value containment / significant-token) plus transform-aware laundering detection (base64/percent/hex) so encoded exfil raises suspicion instead of hiding; every finding names the two seq numbers it spans. 9-rule catalog in 5 families — CHAIN (CHAIN01 realized untrusted->exfil chain, CHAIN02 laundered exfil), SSRF (SSRF01 metadata/private-host, SSRF02 dangerous scheme), INJ (INJ01 into the borrowed LLM's sampling prompt, INJ02 into a user-facing elicitation message, INJ03 concealed zero-width/bidi/TAG Unicode crossing a channel), PROV (PROV02 borrowed-LLM sampling output auto-acted into a tool-call arg with no user turn), AMP (AMP01 one untrusted value fanning out to >=3 sinks) — severity-weighted score + grade + CI exit-code gate, pure stdlib. Ships a benign multi-channel reference capture that exercises an outbound URL sink yet scores 100/A (requires a real flow, not a risky-looking sink) and a trojan capture with 9 findings across all five families incl. 5 CRITICALs (AWS-key resource->URL exfil, tool-result->sampling injection, base64-laundered token exfil, autocomplete->169.254.169.254 metadata-SSRF resource read = CHAIN01+SSRF01), 45 tests. Honest prior-art note: adjacent trace-taint/IFC work exists (canary credential propagation, offline trace provenance, CaMeL/FIDES); the wedge is MCP-channel-typed + passive-over-a-captured-session + LLM-free/dependency-free.

rampart - offline, dependency-free (pure-stdlib) transport-layer hardening prober & auditor for the MCP Streamable HTTP transport: the series' second DYNAMIC entry (after #011 gauntlet drove stdio) and its first on the HTTP transport / perimeter layer - every prior entry audits a message/content channel or a static manifest, and #016 deputy audits the OAuth authorization semantics, not the raw transport hardening (Origin/Host validation, DNS rebinding, bind address, session-ID entropy/format, CORS, protocol-version header). Grounded in the most-CVE'd real MCP vuln class of 2026 - DNS rebinding against local MCP HTTP servers (CVE-2026-11624, CVE-2026-35568 Java SDK, CVE-2026-63118 Ruby SDK, CVE-2026-34742 Go SDK, CVE-2025-66416 Python SDK, CVE-2025-49596 Inspector CVSS 9.4; Backslash 'NeighborJack' 0.0.0.0-by-default, BlueRock 36.7%/7k SSRF). Operationalizes the MCP spec's three-line transport 'Security Warning' plus the Mcp-Session-Id and MCP-Protocol-Version contracts as a battery of active HTTP probes, each isolating ONE property (the foreign-Origin probe sends a legitimate Host/version/session so a finding points only at Origin validation). Clean split of observation from judgement: prober.py (the only networked module) emits a normalised ProbeReport; analyzer.py is a pure, deterministic ProbeReport->[Finding] engine (no net/clock/randomness), so a LIVE probe and a RECORDED report grade through the identical path (probe vs audit), every rule is unit-testable, and captures can be committed and re-audited in CI without a live server. 24-rule catalog in 6 families - RBND (DNS rebinding / Origin & Host validation: RBND01 foreign Origin accepted + RBND02 foreign Host accepted = CRITICAL, RBND03 suffix/substring-bypass, RBND04 Origin:null, RBND05 missing-Origin=INFO since browsers always attach Origin cross-origin so it never penalizes CLI-friendly servers), CORS (CORS03 credentialed wildcard = CRITICAL, CORS01 wildcard ACAO, CORS02 reflected Origin, CORS04 wildcard methods/headers), SESS (Mcp-Session-Id integrity: SESS01 sequential/predictable, SESS02 low-entropy <64bit, SESS03 non-visible-ASCII outside 0x21-0x7E, SESS04 not-unique, SESS05 client-supplied session accepted = fixation, SESS06 missing-session accepted, SESS07 embeds decodable epoch/counter), XPORT (XPORT01 cleartext to remote, XPORT02 NeighborJack non-loopback bind, XPORT03 no-auth on remote, XPORT04 verbose stack-trace disclosure), VER (VER01 invalid MCP-Protocol-Version not 400), CONF (CONF01 GET-without-SSE not 405, CONF02 notification not 202) - severity-weighted score + grade + CI exit-code gate. Ships two byte-stable reference servers sharing one handler and differing only by a Policy dataclass (rampart's whole thesis: safe-vs-catastrophic is defaults, not code): a HARDENED server scoring a clean 100/A and a VULNERABLE server with 15 ground-truth findings incl. 3 CRITICALs (RBND01 foreign-Origin, RBND02 DNS-rebinding foreign-Host, CORS03 credentialed wildcard), 60 tests

escapement - offline, LLM-free, dependency-free (pure-stdlib) auditor for dangerous terminal-control / ANSI escape sequences in server-controlled MCP session content: the series' first entry on the TERMINAL-RENDERING / client-display layer. Every prior entry audits an MCP protocol channel (011-022), a static manifest (001-010), or the HTTP transport (#023 rampart); escapement audits what the terminal EMULATOR renders when a CLI agent (Claude Code, aider, ...) prints untrusted server text to stdout, plus what that text does to the system CLIPBOARD and the client's STDIN. Deliberately distinct from #004 context-xray, which scans manifests for invisible-Unicode aimed at the LLM's PERCEPTION - escapement targets a different victim (terminal + clipboard + input stream), a different layer (runtime display), and a different byte class (C0/C1/CSI/OSC/DCS control sequences). Grounded in Trail of Bits' 2025 finding that Claude Code performs NO ANSI sanitization of MCP tool descriptions/results, and the DiLLMa / terminal-escape-injection line of work (dgl.cx 10 CVEs, OSC 52 clipboard hijack, DSR answerback->stdin, claude-code issues #17787/#32632). Clean split of observation from judgement: extract.py structurally walks server-originated payloads into Item(seq,channel,path,text); tokenizer.py is a total, round-trippable, 8-bit-C1-aware ANSI/ECMA-48 lexer; analyzer.py is a pure, deterministic [Item]->findings engine (no I/O, clock or RNG) with a stateful token walk for multi-token deceptions, so a live-captured session and a committed fixture grade through the identical path and every rule is unit-testable. Self-defending: every byte of evidence is rendered inert (\xNN) so reading the report can never pwn the reader's terminal. 27-rule catalog in 9 families - CLIP (OSC 52 clipboard: CLIP01 write = CRITICAL silent clipboard hijack, CLIP02 query->stdin), LINK (OSC 8 hyperlinks: LINK01 label/target host mismatch, LINK02 dangerous scheme, LINK03 IP/userinfo/punycode authority), TITLE (TITLE01 window title, TITLE02 OSC 7 cwd, TITLE03 OSC 133/633 forged prompt marker), NOTIFY (NOTIFY01 desktop notification, NOTIFY02 BEL flood), ANSWER (answerback->stdin: ANSWER01 DSR CSI 5n/6n, ANSWER02 Device Attributes, ANSWER03 DECRQSS/ENQ, ANSWER04 XTVERSION/XTWINOPS), HIDE (content hiding: HIDE01 cursor-up line-jump overwrite = the exact Trail-of-Bits payload, HIDE02 mid-line CR, HIDE03 erase, HIDE04 alt-screen, HIDE05 conceal / fg==bg, HIDE06 hide cursor), INPUT (INPUT01 bracketed-paste disabled = pairs with a clipboard write, INPUT02 mouse/focus tracking, INPUT03 DECUDK key remap), DOS (DOS01 RIS/DECSTR reset, DOS02 oversized payload, DOS03 8-bit C1 introducer evasion), LAUNDER (LAUNDER01 base64/percent/backslash-encoded escape introducer, a second-order evasion) - severity-weighted score + grade + CI exit-code gate. Ships a benign reference capture that uses real SGR color, a legit matching-host OSC 8 hyperlink and CRLF endings yet scores 100/A (flags BEHAVIOR, not the mere presence of escape bytes) and a trojan capture with 17 findings across all 9 families incl. a CRITICAL OSC 52 clipboard hijack (base64 'rm -rf ~'), an 8-bit \x9b6n DSR that also trips DOS03, and a base64-laundered OSC 52 = LAUNDER01; 101 tests. Honest prior-art note in README/RESEARCH: the attack class is well-documented and generic ANSI strippers (strip-ansi), one MCP runtime gateway (tirith) and a server-side DAST (Bright) exist, but a read-only, LLM-free, pure-stdlib CLIENT-SIDE auditor/classifier over captured MCP session content with a severity score + CI gate did not.

herald - offline, LLM-free, dependency-free (pure-stdlib) trust & safety auditor for the A2A (Agent2Agent) AgentCard served at /.well-known/agent-card.json: the series' first entry on the agent-to-AGENT interoperability layer (experiments 001-024 all audit MCP / a static MCP-or-skills manifest / the MCP HTTP transport / terminal rendering). Audits the discovery & identity artifact a host agent fetches from a remote agent, caches, and injects VERBATIM into its delegation-planning LLM context - the exact mechanism Agent Card Poisoning (Keysight/SemiEngineering, Mar 2026) exploits. Clean split of observation (loader = the only filesystem module) from judgement (analyzer = a pure AgentCard->[Finding] transform with no I/O, clock or RNG) so a live-fetched card and a committed CI fixture grade through the identical path and every rule is unit-testable. 37-rule catalog in 7 families - TRUST (AgentCardSignature JWS/RFC7515 trust root: TRUST01 unsigned, TRUST02 alg:none forgeable = CRITICAL, TRUST03 symmetric HMAC alg, TRUST04 no key reference, TRUST05 malformed protected header, TRUST06 x5u/jku key-URL SSRF/off-origin = CRITICAL, TRUST07 served-but-unverified, TRUST08 provider/endpoint split identity), INJ (Agent Card Poisoning: INJ01 instruction-override text = CRITICAL, INJ02 external endpoint URL smuggled into prose, INJ03 imperative exfiltration phrasing, INJ04 template/variable-substitution syntax, INJ05 embedded tool-call/JSON-RPC snippet), PERC (perception & concealment: invisible/zero-width/TAG, bidi override, C0/C1 control, homoglyph/mixed-script identity impersonation, oversized context-bomb), SEC (security-scheme legality & credential hygiene: SEC01 literal embedded secret = CRITICAL, apiKey-in-query-string, HTTP Basic, cleartext/private OAuth endpoint, deprecated implicit flow, scope-less flow, exposed surface with no auth requirement), XPORT (endpoint transport & SSRF: cleartext service, XPORT02 private/link-local/cloud-metadata endpoint = CRITICAL SSRF/confused-deputy, dangerous scheme, userinfo authority, punycode/IDN host, transport-with-no-interface, unsafe ancillary URL), CONF (bad protocolVersion, schema legality, unknown transport token, ungated authenticated extended card) and LAUNDER (LAUNDER01 base64/percent/hex payload decoding to an injection signature or unsafe URL, a second-order evasion) - severity-weighted score + grade + CI exit-code gate, pure stdlib. Ships a clean reference card (signed ES256+kid, https everywhere, scoped OAuth authorization-code flow, no URLs/instructions in prose) that scores 100/A with ZERO findings and a trojan hotel-booking card (Cyrillic-homoglyph brand impersonation, IGNORE-ALL-PREVIOUS-INSTRUCTIONS + send-conversation-and-api_key-to-attacker payload concealed with zero-width/bidi/BEL, alg:none signature whose x5u key URL is the 169.254.169.254 cloud-metadata endpoint, cleartext link-local API interface, leaked AWS key + JWT, query-string API key, deprecated implicit flow, base64-laundered second exfil URL) that trips all 7 families and scores 0/F with 41 findings, 90 tests. Honest prior-art note: generic prompt-injection scanners, JWS/JOSE validators and SSRF URL classifiers exist independently; the wedge is a single A2A-schema-aware, offline, LLM-free, dependency-free auditor unifying signature-trust + card-poisoning + perception + scheme hygiene + endpoint SSRF + conformance + encoded-launder over one AgentCard with a severity score and CI gate.

recoil - offline, LLM-free, dependency-free (pure-stdlib) auditor for the A2A (Agent2Agent) push-notification / webhook callback channel: the series' second A2A entry (after #025 herald, which audited the STATIC AgentCard identity/discovery artifact) and its first on the A2A RUNTIME callback lifecycle. Audits a captured push-notification exchange - the PushNotificationConfig{url,token,authentication} registrations a host agent makes against a remote agent's tasks PLUS the outbound webhook deliveries the remote agent fires at those URLs and the JWTs it presents - from BOTH the server-side (the A2A spec's own explicit 'servers SHOULD NOT blindly POST to a client URL' SSRF / DDoS-amplifier warning) and the receiver-side (unauthenticated/forged task-status notifications spliced into the host's planning-LLM context) angles. Clean split of observation from judgement mirroring #023 rampart: DNS resolution lives in the capture as resolvedIps (an optional --resolve is the only networked code, quarantined in loader.py) so the analyzer is a PURE, clockless PushCapture->[Finding] transform - a live-captured session and a committed CI fixture grade through the identical path and every rule is unit-testable offline; JWT exp/iat are checked against each delivery's recorded receivedAt, not a wall clock. Self-defending like #024 escapement: every byte of evidence is rendered inert. 34-rule catalog in 8 families - SSRF (webhook target aimed internal: SSRF01 cloud-metadata 169.254.169.254 = CRITICAL, SSRF02 private/loopback/link-local/ULA via literal-or-resolved IP = CRITICAL, SSRF04 decimal/hex/octal-packed IP, SSRF05 IPv4-mapped IPv6, SSRF06 userinfo-authority confusion), REBIND (register-vs-deliver DNS divergence: REBIND01 registered-public/delivered-internal = CRITICAL the validated-once rebind flip, REBIND02 host straddling public+internal, REBIND03 resolution changed), XPORT (transport: XPORT01 cleartext http = CRITICAL, XPORT02 dangerous scheme file:/gopher: = CRITICAL, XPORT03 token smuggled into the URL query/fragment), AUTH (receiver caller-auth: AUTH01 no auth declared, AUTH02 scheme none, AUTH03 delivery presented none though config required it, AUTH04 weak/guessable token, AUTH05 token reused across distinct task/url sinks, AUTH07 inline credentials), JWT (the spec's signed-JWT delivery contract: JWT01 alg:none = CRITICAL, JWT02 symmetric HMAC on a cross-party webhook, JWT03 missing iss/aud/iat/exp/jti/taskId, JWT04 expired-at-receipt, JWT05 audience not bound to the webhook, JWT06 taskId-claim mismatch = cross-task replay, JWT07 no jti = no replay protection, JWT08 attacker-controlled jku/x5u key-source URL = CRITICAL forged-token self-verify), LIFE (lifecycle & amplification: LIFE01 unsolicited/unknown-config delivery, LIFE02 late registration on an already-terminal task, LIFE03 replayed jti, LIFE04 webhook fan-out DDoS-amplifier, LIFE05 duplicate body), INJ (delivered payload injected back into the LLM: INJ01 instruction-override text, INJ02 zero-width/bidi/TAG concealment, INJ03 dangerous URL in payload, LAUNDER01 base64/hex/percent-encoded SSRF/injection) and CONF (PushNotificationConfig schema conformance) - severity-weighted score + grade + CI exit-code gate, pure stdlib (ipaddress/urllib/base64/unicodedata). Ships a benign reference capture (single scoped https webhook, asymmetric ES256 JWT with all six claims bound to the webhook + task, stable public resolution) that scores 100/A with ZERO findings and a trojan capture that trips all 8 families and scores 0/F with 29 findings incl. 7 CRITICALs (metadata-SSRF over cleartext, DNS-rebind registered-1.1.1.1/delivered-10.0.0.5, alg:none delivery JWT whose jku is the 169.254.169.254 metadata endpoint, userinfo-authority metadata SSRF), 97 tests. Honest prior-art note: webhook-SSRF hardening, JOSE/JWT validators and SSRF URL classifiers exist independently and the attack classes are documented (the A2A spec's own SSRF/DDoS warning, the Plane 169.254.169.254 webhook advisory GHSA-fpx8-73gf-7x73, DNS-rebind-at-delivery); the wedge is a single A2A-push-schema-aware, offline, LLM-free, dependency-free auditor unifying webhook SSRF + register/deliver rebinding + transport + receiver-auth + the signed-JWT delivery contract + lifecycle amplification + delivered-content injection over one captured exchange with a severity score and CI gate; the official a2a-inspector is a LIVE debugger that explicitly skips push-notification and security checks

vitrine - offline, LLM-free, dependency-free (pure-stdlib) static auditor for MCP Apps (SEP-1865, spec 2026-01-26) UI resource bundles: the series' first entry on the CLIENT-SIDE RENDERING / web-application layer - every prior entry audits a JSON message channel (011-022), a static manifest (001-010), the HTTP transport (#023 rampart), terminal rendering (#024 escapement) or A2A (#025 herald, #026 recoil); vitrine audits the actual HTML+JavaScript a server ships for the host to render *inside the assistant's own surface*. The wedge is relational: MCP Apps is the one MCP surface where the server DECLARES its capability envelope (_meta.ui.csp connect/resource/frame/baseUriDomains, permissions, visibility, prefersBorder) and separately SHIPS the code, and the spec makes the host's policy a pure function of that declaration ('Host MAY further restrict but MUST NOT allow undeclared domains') - so a declared-vs-observed diff is a conformance check, not a heuristic. Grounded in the fact that a View is not a page but an MCP CLIENT holding a privileged bridge (tools/call, resources/read, ui/update-model-context, ui/message, ui/open-link): markup injection here inherits authority to act as the user, and Backslash's analysis of the 2026-07-28 spec notes these attacks 'operate entirely on the endpoint... None of this touches the network', so MCP gateway/proxy tooling is structurally blind to them. 42 rules / 6 families - DECL (ui:// scheme, fixed text/html;profile=mcp-app MIME, dangling/orphan resources, visibility+permission legality, self-supplied meta CSP), CSP (two-way egress diff over markup+CSS+script origins: undeclared reach AND declared-but-unused excess, wildcard/scheme-only/cleartext/wildcard-subdomain/base-uri), EXFIL (tool-result data reaching a network call, capability API without its permission, cross-origin form post, runtime-computed destination), BRIDGE (postMessage '*' targetOrigin, listener without event.origin, reserved ui/notifications/sandbox-* spoofing, ui/update-model-context fed untrusted data = prompt injection from inside the sandbox, agent-driving without a user gesture, parent.document frame escape), SINK (innerHTML/eval/string-timer fed tool data, weighted by the bridge the injected code inherits) and FACADE (credential fields, host-chrome mimicry = the documented VS Code auth-prompt UI-mimicry attack, inheritance-aware invisible instruction text, full-viewport clickjack overlay, nested remote iframe). Technical core: it LEXES JavaScript rather than grepping it - comments, all three string forms, template literals with recursive interpolation and regex literals (disambiguated from division) are blanked offset-for-offset so every line number stays true and a token inside a comment or string is never a call, while URLs and bridge method names are recovered exactly from a side table. Severity score + grade + CI exit-code gate; ships a conformant bundle (0 findings, 100/A - the catalog's false-positive gate) and a hostile bundle with 41 documented ground-truth defects across all six families incl. 6 CRITICALs (sandbox-proxy spoofing, parent.document escape, wildcard connect domain, tool-result exfiltration, eval of tool data, credential harvesting), 221 tests

penumbra - offline, LLM-free, dependency-free (pure-stdlib) deterministic CACHE-COHERENCE MODEL CHECKER for the MCP 2026-07-28 caching model (SEP-2549: ttlMs + cacheScope on tools/list, prompts/list, resources/list, resources/templates/list, resources/read, server/discover): the series' first entry that answers a question about TIME rather than about an ARTIFACT, and its first whose core is a SIMULATOR rather than a parser or prober. Experiments 001-010 analyse a static manifest, 011-022 audit one message channel, #023 rampart probes the HTTP transport, #024 escapement audits terminal rendering, #025 herald and #026 recoil audit A2A, #027 vitrine audits an MCP Apps UI bundle - every one asks 'is this document/message/bundle safe?'. penumbra's input is not an artifact but a TIMELINE, and its output is a set of intervals with counterexamples inside them. The wedge: caching only became normative on 2026-07-28, and the spec states the hazard itself ('TTL is a freshness hint, not a guarantee. Servers MAY change the underlying data before the TTL expires'). Existing rug-pull defences (Vercel AI SDK fingerprintTools/detectToolDrift ai@7.0.19, ETDI arXiv:2506.01333, and this series' own #008 contravene and #010 capsule) all compare two OBSERVATIONS, so they are structurally blind to the interval in which no second observation happens - and ttlMs is precisely the knob that sets that interval's length. A server may legally publish ttlMs=3600000 and never advertise listChanged, making every definition change guaranteed-unseen for an hour: a spec-legal scheduled rug pull (TRUST04). Grounded in five independent real stale-cache defects predating the spec (claude-code #13646 ignores tools/list_changed, claude-code #38324 caches tools/list indefinitely, codex #33266 stale deferred tool cache, theia #17321 stale tool refs injected into the system prompt, hermes-agent #16764 list_changed RPC races), each shipped as a named client profile. Clean split of observation from judgement mirroring #023 rampart: engine.py is a discrete-event simulator on a virtual integer-ms clock (mutations, notification deliveries, TTL polls and agent actions merged into one totally-ordered log with fixed same-instant priority) that RECORDS belief-vs-truth pairs and never judges; analyzer.py is a pure Timeline->[Finding] transform with no I/O, clock or RNG, so a committed fixture and a freshly built scenario grade through identical code and every rule is unit-testable. Both POINT evidence (an action proving a defect occurred) and INTERVAL evidence (a divergence window proving how long the client was wrong and whether it could ever self-heal) are first-class, with window findings deduplicated across overlapping cache entries. 33 rules in 7 families - PHANTOM (client acts on an already-removed primitive: PHANTOM01 call to a removed tool, PHANTOM04 phantom offered to the model, PHANTOM05 unbounded window), ECLIPSE (blind to something that exists: ECLIPSE01/02/03 incl. windows that can never close), DRIFT (contract moved under a stable name: DRIFT01 superseded schema, DRIFT02 missing new required arg, DRIFT03 narrowed enum/type, DRIFT04 the rug-pull-invisible window, DRIFT05 no revalidate-on-error), TRUST (the security core: TRUST01 CRITICAL auto-approval granted on a stale readOnlyHint = cache staleness converted into unreviewed write authority, TRUST02 became destructive while cached, TRUST03 gained open-world reach, TRUST04 spec-legal invalidation-free window, TRUST05 authority weakened with no re-approval boundary), SCOPE (SCOPE01 CRITICAL public cacheScope on a demonstrably context-varying list, SCOPE02 CRITICAL entry served across authorization contexts with differing ground truths, SCOPE03 private result in a shared cache, SCOPE04 non-uniform scope across pages, SCOPE05 absent scope), CONF (CONF01 negative ttlMs, CONF02 absent hint, CONF03 hints on a non-cacheable MRTR result, CONF04 cached response served for differing request params, CONF05/06 TTL-as-polling-interval without jitter, CONF07 client ignores the hint) and PAGE (PAGE01 duplicate across pages, PAGE02 entry skipped, PAGE03 no consistent snapshot - offset-window shifts from mutations landing mid-fetch) - severity-weighted score + grade + CI exit-code gate. Ships a clean reference scenario that caches for 5 minutes, paginates, serves two tenants and mutates three times mid-session yet scores 100/A with ZERO findings (the catalog's false-positive gate: it flags BEHAVIOUR, never the mere presence of a cache) and a hostile scenario scoring 0/F with 29 findings across all 7 families incl. 3 CRITICALs (public-scope cross-tenant leak, tenant-a entry served to tenant-b, auto-approval on a 490s-stale readOnlyHint), plus a matrix command grading one server policy against all 7 client profiles at once - which shows even a spec-conformant client cannot escape a hostile server policy. 160 tests. Honest prior-art note in README/RESEARCH: cache-coherence model checking is decades old (Joshi/Lamport TLA+), tool-drift detection ships in the Vercel AI SDK today, and multi-tenant cache-isolation auditing is a known gateway concern; the wedge is a single MCP-caching-model-aware, offline, LLM-free, dependency-free simulator that answers the temporal question those cannot - for how long, and in exactly which ways, will this client act on a contract the server has already replaced. Stated limitation: it confirms rather than searches (no timeline-space exploration); a TLA+ encoding was considered and rejected on maintenance, discretisation and output-shape grounds.

contrail - offline, LLM-free, dependency-free (pure-stdlib) BIDIRECTIONAL auditor for the MCP TRACE-CONTEXT / TELEMETRY PROPAGATION PLANE (SEP-414, Final 2026-07-28: _meta.traceparent / _meta.tracestate / _meta.baggage): the series first entry on the OBSERVABILITY plane. Every prior entry audits the PAYLOAD - a static manifest (001-010), one message channel (011-022), the HTTP transport (#023 rampart), terminal rendering (#024 escapement), A2A (#025 herald, #026 recoil), an MCP Apps UI bundle (#027 vitrine) or the caching timeline (#028 penumbra) - and asks is this document/message/bundle safe? contrail audits the METADATA ENVELOPE that rides alongside every single request, and asks a directional question instead: what is leaving, and what am I accepting? The wedge: SEP-414 makes these three the ONLY keys in _meta exempt from reverse-DNS namespacing, they are attached automatically by the tracing SDK and propagated to every peer, and the SEPs entire Security Implications section is two sentences (trace context may include correlation IDs; follow existing data-handling guidance) - while the two W3C specs it incorporates are far sharper (W3C Baggage: application owners MUST ensure no proprietary information crosses trust boundaries via baggage; W3C Trace Context: forged trace headers enable DoS and tracestate reveals your monitoring stack), and an MCP server IS a trust-boundary crossing by construction. Grounded in a shipped 2026 CVE class: the baggage extract path had no item/byte limits in dd-trace-py/-js/-go/-rb/-dotnet (CVE-2026-50271..50276) and opentelemetry-rust (GHSA-w9wp-h8wv-79jx). Trust is a DECLARED input, not a guess (first-party / third-party / unknown), because the same bag is correct hygiene to an internal gateway and a critical leak to a vendor. Clean split of observation from judgement mirroring #023/#026: loader.py is the only filesystem module, everything downstream is a pure Capture->[Finding] transform with no I/O, clock or RNG, so a committed fixture and a live capture grade identically and all 42 rules are unit-testable. Self-defending like #024: every evidence byte is rendered inert. 42 rules / 7 families - LEAK (egress classification across the boundary: LEAK01 credential-shaped value = CRITICAL, PII, internal host, path disclosure, tenant id to a third party, high-entropy token, LEAK07 base64/hex/percent laundered secret, secret parked in a tracestate vendor entry), BOUND (propagation-scope policy rather than value sensitivity: baggage reaching a third party unscrubbed, byte-identical bag broadcast across trust classes, unclassified peer, cleartext, accretion, BOUND06 peer-planted member relayed to another peer = the telemetry confused deputy), PARSE (W3C conformance both directions: malformed traceparent, all-zero ids, forbidden ff / future-version 55-char rule, 32-member tracestate cap, grammar violations, baggage-octet and bare-percent violations, duplicate keys), DOS (the CVE class, ingest-only: 64-member and 8192-byte propagation limits, token bomb, percent-decode amplification / nested list bomb, 512-char tracestate budget), GRAFT (trace integrity - a callee CONTINUING your trace is correct and never flagged: GRAFT01 untrusted peer substitutes its own trace root, first-party orphaned span, forced sampled bit = billing DoS, trace-id reused across principals or sessions, low-entropy/counter-like trace-id), INJECT (the channel reaches high-trust destinations while being reviewed by nothing: INJECT01 CR/LF where SEP-2028 forwards _meta into outbound HTTP headers = header injection CRITICAL and the catalogs one posture-conditional rule, instruction-override text inbound incl. base64-decoded, invisible/bidi/TAG Unicode, ANSI/C0 log forging, structured-log delimiter breakout, metadata/SSRF-shaped URL) and CORR (privacy: PII used as a KEY - indexed even when values are redacted, tracestate naming your observability vendors to a third party, two principals commingled in one propagated context, topology disclosure) - severity-weighted score + grade + CI exit-code gate. Ships a clean reference capture that is deliberately NOT trivial (real baggage, two-vendor tracestate, one trace continued across an internal gateway AND a live third-party peer) scoring 100/A with ZERO findings purely because the client scrubs baggage+tracestate at the boundary and sends the third party only traceparent - a test asserts that property directly so the fixture cannot go clean for the wrong reason - and a hostile capture scoring 0/F with 81 findings across all 7 families incl. 9 CRITICALs, generated by a committed build_hostile.py whose output a test re-derives and diffs; another test FAILS if any of the 42 rules is not exercised by it. 336 tests, weighted toward negative cases (a UUID must not read as an opaque token; a callee continuing your trace must not read as grafting). Honest prior-art note: secret/PII/SSRF classifiers, JOSE validators and W3C parsers all exist independently, the baggage DoS is a documented CVE class, the trust-boundary rule is in the W3C spec itself, and OWASPs MCP08:2025 telemetry entry covers the OPPOSITE problem (telemetry being absent); the wedge is the assembly - a single MCP-_meta-aware, trust-boundary-typed, bidirectional auditor over one captured session. Stated limitations: trust classification is an input not a discovery, it confirms rather than searches, classifiers are pattern-based, and no SDK capture shim ships here

janus - offline, LLM-free, dependency-free (pure-stdlib) DIFFERENTIAL auditor for the MCP HEADER-MIRRORING PLANE (SEP-2243, Final; MCP 2026-07-28): the series' first entry on the plane where the protocol says the same thing TWICE. Every prior entry audits one representation - a static manifest (001-010), one message channel (011-022), the HTTP transport hardening (#023 rampart), terminal rendering (#024 escapement), A2A (#025 herald, #026 recoil), an MCP Apps bundle (#027 vitrine), the caching timeline (#028 penumbra) or the telemetry envelope (#029 contrail) - and asks 'is THIS artifact safe?'. janus asks an AGREEMENT question instead: two components both read this one request, do they read the same thing? The wedge: 2026-07-28 mirrors body values into HTTP headers (Mcp-Method<-method, Mcp-Name<-params.name|uri, and x-mcp-header promoting chosen TOOL-CALL ARGUMENTS into Mcp-Param-{Name}) precisely so gateways, WAFs and load balancers can route, meter and AUTHORIZE without parsing the body - the textbook precondition for a request-smuggling-shaped defect. The spec's only defence is one MUST bound to the LAST component in the chain (servers that process the body MUST reject header/body mismatches, 400 + -32020 HeaderMismatch), protecting a decision the FIRST component already made; and SEP-2243 itself admits header values 'originate from tool call arguments, which may be influenced by an LLM' and MUST NOT be trusted for security decisions - a prohibition stated in prose and enforced by nothing. Reconstructs BOTH readings of each captured request (HeaderView = what a body-blind intermediary believes, BodyView = what the origin will execute) and takes the trust TOPOLOGY as a declared input, so severity escalates only when a security decision actually keys on the header that diverged (the same Mcp-Name mismatch is a curiosity behind a dumb load balancer and an authz bypass behind a tool-allowlisting gateway). Ships the sentinel codec TWICE on purpose - read_strict (spec-exact) and read_lenient (the forgiving decoder real proxies ship: case-insensitive markers, repaired base64 padding) - so their disagreement IS the finding. Observation split from judgement like #023/#029: loader.py is the only filesystem module, everything downstream is a pure Capture->[Finding] transform with no I/O, clock or RNG, asserted STRUCTURALLY by a test that parses each pure module's imports. Self-defending like #024: every evidence byte rendered inert. 60 rules / 7 families - MIRROR (plane divergence: method/name/param/version, MIRROR05 divergence CONCEALED inside a base64 sentinel = invisible to any byte-comparing intermediary, case-only, numeric-only, MIRROR08 whitespace-only as an INFO false-positive gate since the spec requires the server to ACCEPT it, ambiguous name|uri source), SMUGGLE (parser differentials: duplicate Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name/Mcp-Param with differing values = first-wins vs last-wins, differing name spellings, raw CR/LF/NUL, unencoded non-ASCII, unencoded edge whitespace, malformed base64 that strict rejects and lenient recovers, SMUGGLE09 non-lowercase =?BASE64? markers = a literal to the spec but decodable to a lenient reader, SMUGGLE10 unencoded sentinel-shaped literal), ENFORCE (did the origin do the MUST: ENFORCE01 mismatch ACCEPTED = CRITICAL, the single omission that voids every upstream policy at once, missing required header accepted, wrong code/status, ENFORCE05 the stale -32001 that PR #2907 renumbered to -32020, illegal chars accepted, undecodable sentinel accepted, rejection message reflecting raw attacker bytes), XPARAM (annotation integrity incl. a real STATIC-REACHABILITY walker over JSON Schema - the chain must consist solely of 'properties' keys and may not pass through items/composition/conditional/$ref - plus empty/tchar/control names, case-insensitive collisions, non-primitive and number types, JS-unsafe integer bounds, unbounded strings, and XPARAM01 an UNCONSTRAINED MODEL-CONTROLLED parameter feeding a policy-bearing header), POLICY (topology soundness: POLICY01 a header-based policy with NO validating component anywhere = CRITICAL, no protocol-version gate, POLICY03 a security decision keyed on an LLM-sourced Mcp-Param = CRITICAL, meter/quota attributed to the wrong subject, stripping unrecognised Mcp-Param, latent no-validator topology), LEAK (the mirroring plane as EGRESS into every proxy access log: credential-shaped value, PII, local path in Mcp-Name, LEAK04 a secret wrapped in base64 = no confidentiality gained but log secret-scanners now miss it, oversized value, high-entropy token) and CONF (Accept, required headers, orphan/omitted/phantom Mcp-Param, legacy Mcp-Session-Id|Last-Event-ID) - severity-weighted score + grade + CI exit-code gate (0 clean / 1 findings / 2 unreadable input). Ships a conformant capture that is deliberately NOT trivial (mirrors a parameter, legitimately base64-encodes a non-ASCII argument, routes on Mcp-Method AND authorizes on Mcp-Param-Region) yet scores 100/A purely because the origin validates and the gateway re-derives the region decision from the authenticated principal - two tests assert those properties directly and two more flip each one and assert it then FAILS, so the fixture cannot go green for the wrong reason - and a hostile capture scoring 0/F with 80 findings across all 7 families incl. 19 CRITICALs, generated by a committed build_hostile.py whose output a test re-derives and diffs; another test FAILS if any of the 60 rules is unexercised by the fixtures. 442 tests, weighted toward negative cases (a legitimate sentinel must not read as smuggling; identical duplicate headers are not a differential; a whitespace-only difference must not oblige rejection; Mcp-Name must never be entropy-scored because its content is dictated by the spec). Honest prior-art note: differential analysis of two HTTP parsers is mature (HTTP Garden arXiv:2405.17737) and the bug class shipped as 2026 CVEs (@hapi/content CVE-2026-44974 duplicate-parameter smuggling, python-hyper/h2 CVE-2026-71554 duplicate Host, Go HTTP/2 CVE-2026-2219), while header/body consistency is a MUST in the spec itself; the wedge is the assembly - MCP-aware, topology-typed, two-readers-of-one-request, plus a static x-mcp-header graph audit and an egress view. Stated limitations: topology is a declared input not a discovery, it confirms rather than searches, classifiers are pattern-based, the lenient reader is a model not a census, and no capture shim ships here

waterline - offline, LLM-free, dependency-free (pure-stdlib) DIFFERENTIAL REACHABILITY analyzer for Agent Skill bundles (SKILL.md progressive disclosure): the series' first entry treating reachability as a property of the RESOLVER rather than of the artifact. Computes the reachable closure four times over one shared, resolver-agnostic candidate set under four resolver models - link (structural refs only), containment (the path-or-basename substring walk that shipping skill scanners actually implement), directive (path tokens governed by an imperative read/run/load verb), agent (permissive upper bound: directory expansion, glob expansion, sibling-relative spellings, runtime-constructed paths, external URLs) - and reports the two set differences that matter: agent MINUS containment = BLIND SPOTS, the audit-runtime gap (arXiv 2605.05274) localized to specific files a scanner never audits but an agent still loads via a directory-scoped instruction, a glob, or a constructed path; and containment MINUS (link UNION directive) = REFERENCE LAUNDERING, files a scanner counts as legitimately referenced only because their basename appears as an incidental substring in a changelog line or a 'do not use this' note - which is how a dormant payload acquires clean provenance. Adds a tiered progressive-disclosure model (tier 0 = always-resident routing surface, tier 1 = SKILL.md body on activation, tier 2+ = transitive closure, tier = BFS depth) producing capability-by-tier inventory (WL-CAPGAP: exec/network/credential/fs-write markers absent from the routing surface the skill is SELECTED on but present in the closure it ADMITS), disclosure amplification (closure bytes vs routing bytes), confinement escapes (../, ~/, absolute, symlink), dark reads (non-statically-resolvable paths and runtime fetches, reported as unknowable rather than resolved), dead weight, reference cycles and chain depth - 14 finding codes in 7 families, severity-weighted score + grade + CI exit-code gate, text/JSON/Graphviz-DOT/Mermaid output, 118 tests, 5 fixture bundles isolating one divergence class each
